coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 5 units (the domain directory itself plus 02.01, 02.02, 02.03, 02.04), 33 files — exactly the expected count. Every file read in full; no sampling. Rubric dimensions 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 are marked N/A across all five units: Problem Clarity, Persona Specificity, Constraint Explicitness, Success Measurability and Competitive Positioning are all owned by meta/problem-statement.md, meta/personas.md, meta/constraints.md and meta/competitive-landscape.md, which the units reference and never redefine ('Personas from meta/personas.md — referenced, never redefined'). That leaves dimensions 3, 7 and 8 applicable per unit — a 15-checkpoint denominator for the whole domain — so the raw ambiguity percentage is dominated by a small number of findings and should not be read as a quality judgement on the prose, which is exceptionally deep. Structural Compliance (8) is clean everywhere: every sub-domain folder has both *-index.md and *-cx.md, every Role Matrix is fully populated, every leaf feature file carries a Role Lens, the domain index Children table matches the actual folder tree, and there are no Classification Gate violations (no folder has fewer than 3 children). Open Question Resolution (7) is clean in three units and ⚠️ in two, solely because of `[PENDING — Step 5]` markers whose deferral target is a pipeline stage that has already completed. All six blocking findings are cross-file contradictions between a decision in one unit and load-bearing prose in another; none is an isolated vagueness. Notably, the two largest cluster on the same root: the close prompt and the credit record both describe the credited party confirming their own credit as the attestation that reaches the top tier, while 02.04.01 D-11 excludes the credited party from the addressable set entirely.

findings.claim: The close prompt gives each contributor a self-confirmation control on their own credit and calls that tap 'the attestation', but 02.04.01 D-11 forbids the credited party from attesting their own credit and excludes them from the addressable set. Under 02.04.01/02.04.02's rules the in-room tap — the product's entire wedge — collects no attestation at all, and rungs 5 and 6 are structurally unreachable from the capture flow.
findings.evidence: 02.02-session-capture/02.02.03-session-close-capture-prompt.md:20 (Role Lens, Musician) — "Receives one card naming only themselves: their roll interval and every contribution attributed to them on this session's delta … One tap confirms the whole card … This tap is the attestation (`02.04.01`) that separates WeJammin's graph from every self-asserted database. … Never sees another contributor's card." | 02.02.03:97 (Happy Path 6) — "Confirmed claims become session-captured + attested credits (`02.01.01`, `02.04.02`)" | CONTRADICTED BY 02.04-attestation-credit-confidence/02.04.01-attestation-request-confirmation.md:251 (D-11) — "**The attester may never be the credited party** — including through a band entity they are a member of | Self-attestation is self-assertion, and `02.04.02` D-03 says self-assertion never raises the tier. **Excluded from the addressable set** rather than rejected at answer time." | 02.04.01:126 (Happy Path 2) — "The addressable set is derived from the session roll (`02.02.01`) … **minus the credited party themselves (D-11)**" | 02.04.01:154 (edge case) — "Their own rows are excluded (D-11) | Their own row shows \"waiting on others\", **never a self-confirm control**" | 02.04.02-provenance-tiers-credit-confidence.md:52 (rung 5 gate) — "≥1 co-present party, **who is neither the asserter nor the credited party**, confirmed the contribution" | 02.04.02:204 (D-08) — "an attestation only counts if the attester is neither the asserter nor the credited party". The domain's own synthesis already sides with 02.04.01: 02.02-session-capture-cx.md:67 — "a contributor confirming *their own* row is a self-assertion, not corroboration."
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent whether the contributor card carries a confirm control at all, and if it does, what its tap records. Under 02.02.03 it is an attestation that produces a rung-6 credit; under 02.04.01 D-11 the control must not exist and the credit stays at rung 4 with a 'waiting on others' state. The only cross-party ask 02.02.03 actually specifies is the optional unchecked reciprocal line for the Producer's row (D-08), so no contributor's own credit ever acquires an independent confirmation in the room.
findings.short_summary: Close-prompt self-confirm tap vs D-11 attester exclusion

findings.claim: 02.01.01's Happy Path and its Attested lifecycle state both state that the named party confirming their own record produces an attestation that re-derives the tier to the highest tier there is. 02.04.02's rung ladder cannot produce that result, because the credited party's own confirmation is excluded from counting.
findings.evidence: 02.01-credit-graph-discography/02.01.01-credit-record-contribution-ledger.md:90-91 (Happy Path 5-6) — "Each named contributor is asked to confirm their own record (`02.04.01`); the Producer's assertion already stands behind it" / "On confirmation the record's evidence gains an attestation and its tier re-derives to session-captured + attested — **the highest tier there is** (`02.04.02`)" | 02.01.01:138 (Record Lifecycle States) — "Attested | **Named party confirmed** (`02.04.01`) | Evidence-describing label (\"confirmed by 4 people present\")" | CONTRADICTED BY 02.04-attestation-credit-confidence/02.04.02-provenance-tiers-credit-confidence.md:204 (D-08) — "**Independence is per human, and an attestation only counts if the attester is neither the asserter nor the credited party**" | 02.04.02:53 (rung 6 gate) — "Rung 4 **and** ≥1 independent co-present confirmation with lag ≤ 7 days" | 02.04.01-attestation-request-confirmation.md:18 (Role Lens, Musician) — "**Cannot attest their own credit (D-11)**"
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent the tier outcome of the modal capture event. Reading 02.01.01, a captured session where every contributor confirms their own row lands every credit at rung 6. Reading 02.04.02 D-08, the same session lands every credit at rung 4 with zero attestations recorded. These produce different public labels, different traversal weights and different rung-gated downstream behaviour (02.08 RIN eligibility, 06.02.02's rung ≥ 5 credential block).

findings.claim: 02.01.02 treats a party-set 'Private' credit as globally suppressed — its URL 404s, it does not exist for a Fan, it is uncounted — while 02.01.05 D-06 renamed that control 'Unlisted' and defines it as page-scoped only, with the credit remaining on the work's ledger, on co-contributors' pages and in the graph.
findings.evidence: 02.01-credit-graph-discography/02.01.05-credit-visibility-embargo.md:46 (Axis B table) — "**Unlisted** | Per credit, per party | Removed from that party's discography page **only** — still on the work's ledger, still on co-contributors' pages, still in the graph" | 02.01.05:270 (D-06) — "Visibility is **two orthogonal axes** … \"Private\" is renamed **Unlisted** and the UI states that the work's ledger still shows the party" | CONTRADICTED BY 02.01.02-public-discography.md:156 (D-08) — "A **Private** or embargoed credit's URL 404s — never 403" | 02.01.02:23 (Role Lens, Fan) — "Sees public-tier records only: **embargoed, Private and no-public-work-identity records do not exist for them — absent, not greyed, not counted (D-09)**" | 02.01.02:80 (edge case) — "Suppressed credit's URL is requested directly … **404** — indistinguishable from never-existed (D-08, `02.01.05` D-04)" | 02.01.02:98 (Suppressed-empty state) — "Credits exist; none visible to this viewer (all **Private** / embargoed / no public work identity)". 02.01.02 (last updated 2026-07-23, the same date as 02.01.05) uses the superseded term 'Private' in eight places and never once uses 'Unlisted'.
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent whether an Unlisted credit is globally suppressed or page-scoped. 02.01.02 D-08's stated rationale for the 404 is 02.01.05 D-04's leak rule, which governs *embargoed* records only — for an Unlisted credit there is nothing to leak, because the credit is public on the work's ledger by construction. Both a global-404 model and a page-scoped model can be built from this text and they produce opposite results for every co-contributor page and every work ledger.
findings.short_summary: 02.01.02 suppresses Unlisted globally; 02.01.05 scopes it to one page

findings.claim: 02.01.02 D-06 and DT-05 justify never publishing a contested marker on the ground that the one case needing a fast public remedy is already solved unilaterally by setting the credit Private, which 'stops the public harm immediately'. 02.01.05 D-06 and DT-12 state in terms that this remedy does not remove the party's name from public view.
findings.evidence: 02.01-credit-graph-discography/02.01.02-public-discography.md:69 (edge case) — "**Party contests a credit naming *them*** (\"I'm not on this record\") | They do not wait for adjudication — they set the credit **Private** on their own page unilaterally (`02.01.05`), **which stops the public harm immediately**" | 02.01.02:114 (DT-05) — "The one case that genuinely needs a fast public remedy — \"I am not on this record\" — is already solved without adjudication: the named party sets it Private unilaterally, today." | 02.01.02:154 (D-06) — "A party contesting a credit *naming them* sets it Private unilaterally (`02.01.05`) — an immediate remedy requiring no adjudication" | CONTRADICTED BY 02.01.05-credit-visibility-embargo.md:50 (D-06 rationale) — "A player who marks a credit Private, expecting it gone, **will find their name on the work's public ledger and on four co-contributors' pages** — because a credit is a **joint** fact that four other people also assert … Calling it Private would be a truth-in-labelling failure that users discover only after they have relied on it." | 02.01.05:231 (DT-12) — "the model was a shippable lie … \"Private\" can only ever be a **page-level opt-out**"
findings.forcedInvention: D-06 — a load-bearing decision that forbids any public contested state anywhere in the domain — rests on a remedy that the owning feature says does not work. The implementer must either build a genuine claimant-side public-suppression control (which 02.01.01 D-11 explicitly refuses as a censorship weapon) or accept that the 'I am not on this record' case has no fast remedy, reopening D-06's cost/benefit. 02.03.03 Q-04 already records the adjacent hole for a second claimant but does not cover the named party.
findings.short_summary: "Set it Private" remedy does not stop the public harm

findings.claim: 02.10's Role Lens grants the Producer Full access and session-level AI disclosure, describing them as the de-facto compliance point, while the same file's D-04 and edge-case table restrict disclosure to a contributor's own work and the domain CX file assigns the AI axis to the named contributor as a per-field ownership split. There is also no session-level disclosure object anywhere in the v1 data model.
findings.evidence: 02.10-ai-contribution-disclosure.md:19 (Role Lens) — "Producer | **Full** | **Discloses at the session level and per contribution.** The de-facto compliance point, because they assemble the record and they are who a label asks." | CONTRADICTED BY 02.10:122 (D-04) — "**You disclose your own contribution only** | Disclosing someone else's work as AI is an assertion about their craft and is defamatory if wrong." | 02.10:71 (edge case) — "Producer discloses AI on someone else's contribution | **Not permitted** … | Own contributions only" | credits-attribution-cx.md:260 (CX-14) — "the Producer owns the attribution on the row, and the *named contributor* owns its AI-disclosure axis (`02.02.02`→`02.10`, D-04) … One row, two owners of two fields." | 02.02-session-capture/02.02.02-per-track-contribution-log.md:109 (edge case) — "Producer tries to set the AI disclosure axis on someone else's contribution | **Refused.** `02.10` D-04". The v1 vocabulary binds disclosure to a contribution only: 02.10:33 — "A disclosure attached to **a contribution** is zero or more involvement entries"; there is no session-scoped disclosure entity in the field table (02.10:35-42) or the States tables (02.10:82-96).
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent (a) whether the Producer may write the AI axis on rows naming other people — a permission the CX file flags as requiring per-field authorization in /write-be-spec — and (b) what a 'session level' disclosure is, since no entity, field, scope value or state exists for one. The Access column reading 'Full' against the Musician's 'Config (own contributions)' is itself the signal that a broader grant was intended.
findings.short_summary: 02.10 Producer session-level disclosure vs D-04 own-only rule

findings.claim: The sub-domain CX file states that an open dispute holds the tier and that a retraction's effect must therefore queue rather than apply — and cites 02.04.02's States table as its authority. 02.04.02 D-10 and its Contested state say the opposite: a contest neither moves nor freezes the rung, and evidence arriving during a contest applies normally with no freeze.
findings.evidence: 02.04-attestation-credit-confidence/02.04-attestation-credit-confidence-cx.md:77 (CX-02, synthesis question 5) — "State transition conflict: Retraction during an open dispute (`02.05`) — **the dispute holds the tier** (`02.04.02` states), so **the retraction's effect must queue** rather than apply underneath the dispute." | CONTRADICTED BY 02.04.02-provenance-tiers-credit-confidence.md:206 (D-10) — "**A contest neither moves nor freezes the rung** | An objection is not evidence (D-02, domain D-08). **A freeze would be a stamp with extra steps and would make opening a dispute a way to lock a rung.**" | 02.04.02:123 (edge case) — "Contest opened on the credit (`02.05`) | The contest **does not move the rung** … Evidence arriving during a contest applies normally: **no freeze** (D-10)" | 02.04.02:144 (Contested state) — "Contest open (`02.05`) | **Rung continues to derive normally.**"
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent whether tier derivation is suspended for the duration of a dispute. Queueing retraction effects gives every party a way to lock a rung by filing a free unilateral contest — precisely the outcome D-10 exists to prevent — while applying them immediately contradicts an explicit 'must' in the sub-domain's own synthesis artifact. Following the citation does not resolve it: the cited States table says the opposite of the claim made about it.
findings.short_summary: CX-02 queues retraction during dispute; D-10 forbids any freeze

findings.claim: 02.02.01 D-09 scopes a Musician's roll visibility to overlapping presence intervals and states that this prevents an asynchronous contributor learning a record's unreleased personnel. 02.01.05 D-14 makes participant status per-session and binary, explicitly rejects interval scoping, and gives every party on the roll sight of the session's embargoed credits — which name the personnel.
findings.evidence: 02.02-session-capture/02.02.01-session-roll-call.md:145 (edge case) — "Async contributor tries to see who else played | They have no overlapping interval, so they see only themselves and the session owner (D-09). **They cannot learn the unreleased personnel of a record they sent one part to**" | 02.02.01:216 (D-09) — "A Musician sees only the roll entries whose intervals **overlap their own**, plus the session owner" | CONTRADICTED BY 02.01-credit-graph-discography/02.01.05-credit-visibility-embargo.md:113 — "The participant set is the session roll (`02.02.01`) — **every party on it**, including those the roll records as present-but-uncredited" | 02.01.05:38 (Axis A table) — "**Embargoed** … Who sees it: **Session participants** + the credited party" | 02.01.05:115 — "**Explicitly rejected: scoping a participant's visibility to the intervals they attended (DT-13).** A dep who played 2pm–3pm sees the session's credits, not a 60-minute slice". The asynchronous contributor is on the roll (02.02.01:124 — "Roll entry marked `remote — asynchronous`"), therefore a participant, therefore entitled to the session's embargoed credits.
findings.short_summary: Interval-scoped roll hides what per-session credit access reveals

findings.claim: The sub-domain CX file still records the sequential wrap→reconcile→prompt→confirmations trigger chain that 02.02.03 D-05 and DT-04 reject as the design's central error. 02.02.03 flags the reconciliation as owed to a stage that has since completed, and the CX text carries no marker of its own.
findings.evidence: 02.02-session-capture/02.02-session-capture-cx.md:56 (CX-02, synthesis question 2) — "Trigger chain: **Wrap signal → reconcile → prompt → per-row confirmations → credit records.**" | CONTRADICTED BY 02.02.03-session-close-capture-prompt.md:206 (D-05) — "**The contributor asks and the Producer's reconciliation are two independently-firing halves.** Both fire within 5 s of the wrap signal; **neither gates the other** … Gating the first on the second inverts the thesis." | 02.02.03:170 (DT-04) — "❌ **REJECTED — this was the design's central error, and it inverted its own thesis.**" | 02.02.03:185 (Cross-Cut Notes) — "**Step 6 must reconcile CX-02's trigger chain against D-05**: CX-02 records \"wrap → reconcile → prompt → confirmations\", which is the sequential model DT-04 rejects. … This is a change to a sibling artifact I do not own, flagged rather than made." The flag names Step 6, a stage the tree's own cross-references treat as complete (02.01.04 Q-01: "Re-pointed from `/ideate-discover` Step 5, which has run").
findings.short_summary: 02.02 CX still carries the sequential chain D-05 rejects

findings.claim: 02.08's Happy Path gates embargoed-credit inclusion on the identity of the export recipient, while its own edge-case table, 02.01.05 and the domain CX gate it on the export's scope. Recipient and scope are different predicates and select different credit sets.
findings.evidence: 02.08-credit-export-ddex-rin.md:50 (Happy Path 4) — "Package generates; **embargoed credits excluded unless the recipient is a participant**" | INCONSISTENT WITH 02.08:59 (edge case) — "Embargoed credits in scope | Excluded by default; **participant-scoped export** may include them" | 02.01-credit-graph-discography/02.01.05-credit-visibility-embargo.md:253 (Cross-Cut Notes) — "**Participant-scoped export may include embargoed credits; catalog-scoped export excludes and says so.**" | credits-attribution-cx.md:25 (CX-10) — "participant-scoped export may carry embargoed credits, catalog-scoped export must exclude and say so" | 02.01.05:207 (CX-10 detail, permission intersection) — "**Scope (participant vs catalog) is the permission that decides whether embargoed rows are eligible at all.**" A RIN's recipient is a label or distributor and is essentially never a session participant, so the Happy Path rule would exclude embargoed credits from every export, including the participant-scoped one 02.01.05 D-09 guarantees the credited party.
findings.short_summary: 02.08 gates embargo on recipient identity, not export scope

findings.claim: 02.02.04 carries a deferral marker whose target is a pipeline stage that has already run and which names no owner, so nothing routes it to a decision-maker.
findings.evidence: 02.02-session-capture/02.02.04-session-attendance-proof.md:49 (edge case, User Sees column) — "Everyone co-signs a fabricated session | … **Accepted cost, stated plainly**: a fully corroborated fiction keeps its top rung indefinitely | `[PENDING — Step 5]`". No owner is named and no Open Question in the file covers it: Q-01 asks whether device/location presence is in scope, Q-02 asks about evidence-trail visibility in a dispute, Q-03 asks about a retention limit (02.02.04:93-95). The file is dated 2026-07-23 and the tree elsewhere treats Step 5 as complete (02.01.04-identifier-resolution-duplicate-merge.md:90 — "Re-pointed from `/ideate-discover` Step 5, which has run and left the corner open").
findings.short_summary: `[PENDING — Step 5]` marker on a completed stage, no owner

findings.claim: 02.03.03 defers the unwinding of a late claim contest's accumulated downstream effects to a completed pipeline stage, with no owner and no Open Question covering it.
findings.evidence: 02.03-claiming-cold-start-seeding/02.03.03-claim-adjudication.md:69 (edge case) — "Claim contested years after attachment | Same path; the credit has by then accumulated **downstream effects (royalty registration, reputation, traversal edges) that must unwind** | `[PENDING — Step 5]`". No owner is named. The file's six Open Questions cover domain ownership (Q-01), claimant identity disclosure (Q-02), unattachable imports (Q-03, resolved), the true owner's lack of control (Q-04), unbounded pendency (Q-05) and the same-name shell page (Q-06) — none covers the unwind (02.03.03:114-119). Contrast the sibling case, which is properly routed: 02.04-attestation-credit-confidence/02.04.03-attestation-retraction.md:91 (Q-03) resolves the analogous royalty unwind by assigning it to domain 10 with a citation.
findings.short_summary: Late-contest downstream unwind deferred to a completed stage
